card.title: Trading bots ask for your keys.
card.sub: Or a balance they can move however they like, and no brake when one goes wrong.

lines: Trading bots ask for a lot of trust: your keys, or a balance they can move however they like. And when one goes wrong, there's no brake.

card.title: Agents can trade now. Who holds the money, and who can stop them?

lines: AI agents can now read markets and place orders. The open question is control: who holds the money, and who can stop them.

segments.label: The solution
segments.sub: A council, inside a limit the chain enforces
lines: XORR is a council of AI agents that trades for you, inside a limit you sign and the chain enforces. Every trade is voted on, seat by seat, and you can replay why.

segments.label: One hold
lines: And one hold stops every agent, on chain, and the app reads it back from the chain.

segments.label: Why Monad
segments.sub: Final in ~0.5 s · receipts with the send
lines: Why Monad? A block is final in about half a second, and a send returns its receipt. So the council votes and fills inside a second, for a tenth of a cent of gas.

segments.label: Built on Monad
lines: It's built on Monad's own features: commit states, the txpool, native staking, and the P256 precompile for passkeys.

card.title: Live, with a transaction behind every claim.

lines: And it's live on Monad testnet: three verified contracts, real council rounds, and real fills on Perpl, each one with its transaction.

card.title: Hire an agent. Set its limit. Stop it with one hold.
card.sub: Next: real users on testnet, and more Monad venues for the council to route to.

lines: The vision: anyone can hire an agent to trade for them, set its limit, and stop it with one hold. Next, we want real users on testnet, and more Monad venues for the council to route to.

card.title: A council of AI agents trades for you on Monad, and one hold stops it on chain.
